extracted.intended_audience: press officers, PR practitioners, and journalists evaluating or crafting press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Use Gans's source-power framework and eight 'enduring values' to evaluate or craft press releases for likelihood of journalistic pickup. The rubric helps PR practitioners tailor releases to newsroom incentives and news-genre norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives and pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the source bring a pre-existing access relationship (regular briefing, embedded correspondent, established beat presence)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists favor sources with ongoing access relationships; releases from organizations that already brief or regularly interact with a newsroom have higher pickup probability. Signal prior contacts or scheduled briefings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of the source
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials, large corporations, and major institutions are reported on at much higher rates than non-elite sources of equal substantive newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make issuer's institutional stature explicit (titles, organization size, regulatory authority). Recognize that elite rank can outweigh equivalent substantive claims from less-known actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to supply suitable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that match the format the news organization can use win pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide facts, quotes, soundbites, visuals, and ready-to-use copy tailored to the outlet's format (TV-friendly bites for evening news, narrative leads for weeklies). Ensure timeliness and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and social proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources physically and socially close to the newsroom are picked up more readily; releases optimized for the issuer's local press cluster have higher conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize pitches (regional hooks, local spokespeople) and emphasize proximity to the outlet's audience or beat reporters to increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources who have proved reliable in the past are favored; releases benefit from issuer reputation, not just current text quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, reference prior accurate interactions or coverage; cultivate and communicate a track record of reliability to build trust with reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability to the news genre
rubrics_metrics.description: A release that fits the network's evening-news arc, or the magazine's weekly cycle, is favored over generic copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor pacing, framing, and content to the outlet's rhythm (daily broadcast, weekly magazine, online quick-take). Fit story into the outlet's expected narrative arc or production timetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnocentrism (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames events in terms of the audience's national/local self-image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how the story reflects or affects the community or nation; use language that ties the news to audience identity or pride when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Altruistic democracy (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Showcases public-spirited behavior or, conversely, public corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight civic virtue, watchdog outcomes, or corruption scandals; frame narratives around public interest and democratic norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible capitalism (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights either responsible business behavior or its failures (this is the value most invoked in business press releases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position corporate news as demonstrating good corporate citizenship or revealing lapses; include financial or governance details that illustrate responsibility or failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-town pastoralism (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Connects national stories to community-scale narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer human-scale, community-focused angles or local exemplars that make broader issues relatable through a local lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualism (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foregrounds individual heroes, victims, or wrongdoers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include named individuals with compelling personal stories to personalize broader trends or events; supply quotes and biographical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderatism (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids extremism; pitches the 'reasonable' middle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories to emphasize balance, moderation, and mainstream perspectives rather than fringe positions to appeal to broad-audience outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social order (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on threats to and restorations of social order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame crises, solutions, enforcement, or recoveries in terms of impacts on public order and safety; clarify symptoms and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National leadership (enduring value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights leaders, especially in their official capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature officials or leaders in their authoritative roles; emphasize decisions, statements, or actions by recognized leaders that signal importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value-anchoring lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the lead invoke one of the eight enduring values explicitly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a lead that signals an enduring value (e.g., individual heroism, local impact, corporate responsibility) to align immediately with journalists' evaluative frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named individual story
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there at least one named individual (researcher, patient, executive) whose story personalizes the announcement (individualism)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one named source with a humanizing anecdote or quote to create a narrative thread reporters can follow and illustrate broader claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order/disorder framing
rubrics_metrics.description: For crisis-related releases, does the language frame the event as either disorder (problem) or restoration (solution) — both newsworthy postures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly frame crises in terms of threat or recovery; spell out consequences and remedies to fit journalists' preference for stories about social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-existing relationship signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release reference prior accurate dealings with the receiving outlet (e.g., 'as we briefed you in [date], the trial has now reported')?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal prior briefings or reliable interactions to leverage existing access relationships and remind journalists of ongoing coverage threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer-rank signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the issuer's institutional rank made obvious (university name, regulatory authority, market-cap rank)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make institutional credentials prominent in the release header or lead to signal elite status and increase perceived newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locality-fit option
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the release distributable in both a national and a locally-customized version (small-town pastoralism)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare versions with local angles, statistics, or spokespeople so the same announcement can be repackaged for local outlets and increase pickup across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined pickup-worthiness predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup increases sharply when the release simultaneously (a) signals the issuer's institutional power, (b) anchors to one or more enduring values, and (c) supplies a personalized narrative thread for the journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to satisfy all three simultaneously: make institutional rank clear, open with an enduring-value lead, and include a named individual or narrative. Combining these elements multiplies pickup probability rather than relying on any single tactic.
